column1: # P115-C. THE COUNTRY -> REGION MAP IS A COMMITTED FILE, NOT A DERIVATION.
# `orgs.region.tsv` (P112-L) made the ORG placement a file. This one does the
# same for the only machine-readable country signal a repository tree carries:
# the top-level domain of an address inside a structured metadata field.
# `region` is the brief's CLOSED vocabulary and nothing else ever appears in
# the region column: North America | EMEA | APAC | LATAM | Global.
# FOUR CLASSES, and only one of them places a row:
#   cc        a country-code TLD whose country sits in exactly one region.
#   cc?       a country-code TLD whose country is assigned to different
#             regions by different conventions (Russia, Turkey, the Caucasus,
#             Central Asia). NEVER PLACES. Reported separately, never folded
#             into a regional total -- the same discipline orgs.region.tsv
#   vanity    a country-code TLD in widespread use as a vanity or
#             P115-D. The trap is real and it is not hypothetical: `youtu.be`
#             is not Belgian, `bit.ly` is not Libyan, `codecov.io` is not in
#             the British Indian Ocean Territory and `shields.io` is not
#             either. A map that reads these as countries does not mis-state
#             one row, it mis-states whichever rows happen to carry a badge.
#             The cost of the class is real too and is measured, not waved
#             away: a genuinely Belgian university address is DROPPED here.
#             An under-count that cannot invent a country is the only kind of
#             error this field tolerates, because `region` is filtered on
#             downstream and a guess does not read as a guess -- it reads as
#   gtld      a generic TLD (.com .org .net .dev .app ...). Carries no
# .edu/.gov/.mil are listed as `cc` -> North America. The basis is
# eligibility, not geography: .edu registration is restricted to
# US-accredited postsecondary institutions and .gov/.mil to US government
# bodies. Stated here because it is the one entry in this file whose region
# comes from a registry POLICY rather than from a country code, and
# P115-G reports what this KB's shelf would read without it.
